findings.title: Rewritten inner loop drops the uncapped `max_neighbors` path
findings.description: The slice-150 kernel handles `max_neighbors <= 0` (the encoding for `ProfileConfig.max_neighbors = None`, verified in `src/migratory/gpu/agent_state.py` `_build_profile_param_table`, which writes `0.0` for unset) with a dedicated accept-all-within-radius sub-branch (`if max_neighbors <= 0: # Uncapped: accept all directly`). The slice's "AFTER (slice 152)" inner loop has no such branch: with `max_neighbors == 0` and `k_nearest` (the new default per §"Default neighbor mode is `k_nearest`"), `heap_size < max_neighbors` is false, and `dsq < heap_dsq[0]` is true for every candidate because `heap_dsq[0]` is initialised to the `INF` sentinel — so the eviction path executes on an empty heap, reads `evicted = heap_idx[0] == -1`, and indexes `_px_c[-1]`. The doc says `radius_only` is "identical to the `k_nearest` uncapped sub-branch … promoted to a first-class mode", which implies uncapped is now only reachable via `radius_only` — but it never states that `max_neighbors` unset + `k_nearest` is invalid, and no error/guard is specified. Per the project convention against silent fallback, this must be either explicitly handled (retain the uncapped branch) or rejected at config/parse time with a clear error.

findings.title: Success criterion 2 misstates the existing parity test's tolerance
findings.description: Criterion 2 claims "the parity test from slice 150 (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_parity.py`) continues to pass. Mean speed and mean nearest-neighbor distance remain within 5% of the numpy reference at N=4500." The shipped test asserts a **20%** relative tolerance (`speed_rel <= 0.20`, `nn_rel <= 0.20`) and runs on `mid-flock` (N=3500), not N=4500. The slice's own Risk 3 names that test as "the regression net" for the heap index-space change, so the stated tolerance is the criterion that would be used to accept or reject the change. As written, implementing the 5% criterion would either require tightening a test the slice does not own or produce a permanent false failure. Restate the actual tolerance and workload, or state explicitly that this slice tightens it and why.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough specifies CLI surface that does not exist
findings.description: Steps 2–5 are the load-bearing gate procedure (step 4 is "THE gate"), and all of them are expressed as commands against a CLI that does not provide them: `src/migratory/bench/cli.py` exposes only `--workload`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir`, `--list-backends`, `--list-workloads` — there is no `parity` subcommand, no `--neighbor-mode`, and no `--ticks`. `neighbor_mode` is currently settable only via the workload YAML (`Workload.from_yaml`, `src/migratory/bench/workload.py`). The doc must either specify the real mechanism for injecting `neighbor_mode: radius_only | k_nearest` into a measured run (new workload YAMLs, or a new flag as explicit scope) or rewrite the commands, otherwise the exit criterion has no executable procedure.

findings.title: Scope beyond the slice-plan entry: new `radius_only` mode, `k_first` removal, and default flip
findings.description: Slice-plan entry 13 assigns this slice the coherent reindex plus the FRNN path ("With coalesced reads, k-nearest via FRNN (collect all within radius R, then partial-sort the small candidate set per thread) becomes viable at scale"), with exit criteria "k-nearest TPS at N=200k within 20% of k-first TPS at the same N; parity preserved; **no regression on k-first path**." The design instead (a) adds a second first-class neighbor mode (`radius_only`) with its own purpose, docs, and benchmark ladder, (b) removes `k_first` entirely from the kernel, `ComputeConfig`, `Workload` and `_NEIGHBOR_MODE_MAP`, (c) flips the default to `k_nearest`, and (d) explicitly defers FRNN to a follow-up slice. Items (a)–(c) are not assigned by the plan entry and invalidate its "no regression on k-first" criterion; (d) defers the mechanism the entry names as this slice's deliverable. Either the plan entry is amended first, or `radius_only`/`k_first` removal/default flip is cut and shipped as a separate slice.

findings.title: Tier target mislabelled and the performance gate has no absolute floor
findings.description: The Overview states this slice makes k-nearest "viable at the architecture's Tier 3 target (N=200k)". The parent architecture defines **Tier 3 as 250k on production-class NVIDIA hardware with server-side frustum culling**, while 200k is characterised in slices 148/145 notes as a dev-class CUDA measurement point (3 TPS at N=200k post-145). The slice's only performance gate (criterion 4, line 358) is relative — `k_nearest_tps >= 0.8 × radius_only_tps` — with no absolute TPS floor. A run where `radius_only` is itself far below any tier milestone passes the gate. Because the parent architecture states TPS milestones for this path, this slice should restate the applicable target with a specific number (even if it is an intermediate target below Tier 3) rather than a relative ratio alone.

findings.title: `profile_index_c` is written every tick and never read
findings.description: The reindex kernel copies `_profile_index` into `_profile_index_c` and `_bind_state_fields` binds it, but nothing reads it: the force kernel's only use of the profile index is `pi = _profile_index[i]` in the outer loop over original-order agents, which the slice explicitly leaves unchanged ("The outer loop … are unchanged"). In-scope item 3 nonetheless lists `_profile_index` among the fields to substitute in the inner loop. This is a dead field — extra per-tick reindex work and 0.8 MB at N=200k (the memhood cost line at 214 sums seven fields, one of which is unused). Cut it from the field set, the reindex body, and the binding.

findings.title: Design weight: reference-reading sections, duplicated FRNN material, and non-gating probes
findings.description: For a plan entry rated "Risk: Medium. Effort: 3/5", the document carries substantial material that is not design of this slice: §"Reference points" (lines 36–44) is background reading on Babylon.js/WebGPU 16M/4M, spatial-hash and brute-force ceilings, and an "implication for targets" argument that is restated again in criterion 4 (line 358) and Future Work (line 456 onward). The FRNN collect-then-sort discussion appears twice (§"Heap is the starting point…", line 187, and Future Work) while the slice explicitly does not implement it. Verification step 5 (lines 395–400, `mid-flock-500k` and `mid-flock-1M`) is explicitly "not a hard gate" and, per the doc's own trigger condition, belongs to the FRNN follow-up slice. Cut the reference-points section to a one-line citation, state the FRNN material once under Future Work, and drop the 500k/1M probe from this slice's verification (or move it to the follow-up) — none of it changes what this slice must build.

findings.title: "Three `neighbor_mode` values to two" is inaccurate
findings.description: The Value section says the slice "does not change any external interface other than collapsing three `neighbor_mode` values to two". The current mode set is already two (`_VALID_NEIGHBOR_MODES = {"k_first", "k_nearest"}` in `quadrants_fused_kernels.py` and `config.py`); the "third" is the uncapped sub-branch inside the kernel, not a config value. Rephrase to avoid an incorrect interface claim.

findings.title: Error type name and field-group wording do not match the code
findings.description: The doc says configs using `k_first` "raise a `ConfigurationError`"; the codebase raises `ValueError` (wrapped to `ConfigError` in `migratory_server/config.py`, plain `ValueError` in `migratory/bench/workload.py`). Separately, Risk 4 (line 427) says the new fields are placed "in the same `qd.root.dense(qd.i, N)` group as the originals", but the code listing at lines 210–226 places the six coherent fields in their own `place()` call and `coherent_to_original` in a third — neither shares the originals' group. Both are minor but should match the implementation the slice will be reviewed against.

findings.title: Prerequisite "shipped on `main`" conflicts with the slice plan's own record
findings.description: Slice 152's Dependencies says "Slice 150 … is shipped on `main` as of 2026-05-05", but slice-plan entry 11 (line 50) is unchecked (`[ ]`) and `150-slice…md` carries `status: in_progress`. Since this slice's design removes `k_first` and depends on 150's heap/pruning internals, the base it builds on should be unambiguous. If 150 has shipped, the plan checkbox and 150's status are stale and should be updated; if it has not, this design is premature.
